featured_reviews.name: Riya Patil
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Granth Book Store in Juhu recently and honestly felt a little disappointed with the overall customer experience. A bookstore is usually expected to feel welcoming and comfortable for readers, but the staff behavior did not reflect that warmth.

While I was casually clicking pictures of the bookstore, one of the helpers stopped me and said photography was not allowed. What felt confusing was that the Google reviews of the same store already contain several visitor-clicked photos. If photography policies exist, they should at least be communicated politely and consistently.
Another uncomfortable part of the experience was the way the staff constantly observed us while we were browsing books, almost as if customers were being viewed with suspicion rather than trust. Browsing peacefully is one of the most enjoyable parts of visiting a bookstore, and unfortunately that comfort was missing here.
The bookstore itself has a lovely collection, which is why I genuinely hope the management works on creating a more welcoming and customer-friendly environment for book lovers.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Thank you for sharing your feedback and for appreciating our book collection.

We are sorry that your experience at Granth Book Store, Juhu did not feel as welcoming as it should have. Creating a comfortable environment for readers is very important to us.

Regarding photography, we do have a “No Photography” signage displayed at the store as part of our guidelines. While we do try to communicate this consistently, there may have been instances where it was missed. We also understand your concern about how the situation may have felt, and we will ensure our team handles such interactions more politely and respectfully.

We are also sorry that you felt observed while browsing. This is certainly not the experience we aim to create for our customers.

Your feedback has been noted seriously, and we will work on improving the overall in-store experience.

We truly appreciate your feedback and hope to welcome you again soon.

featured_reviews.name: Sona Sharma
featured_reviews.review_text:
Granth at Taj Santacruz , Mumbai is a rare gem of a bookstore with an absolute legend of a staff member!

I had the most wonderful experience at the Granth , and I had to leave a review to specifically commend one of its staff member Mr Shubham Mishra  for  his customer service that was nothing short of masterful.

The store itself is a treasure trove—beautifully lit, impeccably clean, and so well-organized that you feel welcomed the moment you step inside. It’s clear a lot of care goes into curating the selection. They have an incredible range of books for every age group, from whimsical children's picture books to thought-provoking literary fiction including a delightful collection of sacred artefacts, tarot cards, and other unique items interspersed throughout. It gives the place a very special, almost magical atmosphere.

While i was busy browsing through the sections of my interest, without being  intrusive in the slightest; Mr Shubham Mishra simply observed from a respectful distance, clearly trying to gauge my interests without disturbing my flow. It was a subtle art—distant, unobtrusive observation—and it was incredibly effective.

After a few minutes, he politely approached. Without any pressure or small talk, he simply said, "If you're interested in that author, you might also appreciate these," and gently placed a set of related books on a table besides me .They were all perfect suggestions, one that showed he truly understood the theme I was exploring.

Then, he did something I wish every bookseller would do: he simply , smiled, and vanished  as quietly as he had appeared giving  me the needed space and silence to browse through the books, to read the first few pages, and to decide for myself if it was the right fit. There was no hovering, no sales pitch—just expert guidance delivered with the utmost respect for the reader's private journey.

This level of attentive, intelligent, and graceful service is incredibly rare. He didn't just sell me the books; he enhanced my entire experience and deepened my love for browsing physical bookstores.

If you're looking for a perfect book or a unique gift in a serene and welcoming environment,with sincere expertise and assistance of Mr Shubham Mishra ,do yourself a favor and visit [Granth The Booktore at Taj Santacruz , Mumbai I know I'll be back.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Then we walked into Crosswords bookstore right next door and realized Third Wave is inside the store, near the counter. There is a decent seating area there, not huge, but enough space to sit comfortably with a coffee.

The bookstore itself is nice. It’s spacious and has a wide range of books and other products. You’ll find books across many genres, along with stationery and gift items. Prices vary a lot. Some books are affordable, while others, especially imported editions, are quite expensive. It really depends on what you pick up and where it’s coming from.

I liked that there were options at different price points. You can browse without feeling rushed, and it doesn’t feel too cramped even when there are people around. The coffee inside makes it a good place to pause for a bit, read a few pages, or just sit quietly.

We were actually looking for Third Wave Coffee and found it on the map. When we reached the building, there was no sign of it anywhere. Nothing in the elevator either, so we were a bit confused at first

Overall, it’s a good bookstore to visit in Juhu if you enjoy browsing and don’t mind spending some time there. Just know that Third Wave Coffee is inside Crosswords and not a separate outlet, which can be confusing at first.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Ashish Book Centre, tucked away near the bustling CSMT Railway Station in Fort, is nothing short of a paradise for true book lovers. In a city that’s always racing against time, this bookstore feels like a quiet, timeless refuge where stories patiently wait to be discovered.

What makes Ashish Book Centre truly special is its incredible collection. From rare second-hand classics and academic textbooks to novels, competitive exam guides, and out-of-print treasures—you never know what gem you’ll stumble upon. Browsing through the shelves feels like going on a literary treasure hunt, and every visit brings a new surprise.

The owners and staff are extremely knowledgeable and helpful. They don’t just sell books; they understand them. Whether you walk in with a specific title in mind or just a vague idea of what you want to read, they guide you with genuine enthusiasm and honesty. Their passion for books is infectious.

Another big win is the affordability. Ashish Book Centre proves that great reading doesn’t have to be expensive. Students, avid readers, and collectors alike will appreciate the fair pricing and excellent condition of the books.

Located in the heart of Fort, just a stone’s throw from CSMT, it’s incredibly convenient and perfectly placed for a spontaneous visit after work or college. Despite the chaos outside, the store offers a calm, almost nostalgic vibe that reminds you why physical bookstores still matter.

If you love books, value knowledge, or simply enjoy the charm of old-school bookstores, Ashish Book Centre is an absolute must-visit. It’s not just a shop—it’s an experience, a legacy, and a reminder that the love for reading is very much alive in Mumbai. 📚

featured_reviews.name: Radhikaa Desai
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited the Geeta Press outlet at Princess Street, Marine Lines for the first time after my marriage, and the experience was truly memorable.🤌✨️ Amidst the busy lanes of South Mumbai, stepping inside felt like entering a small temple of knowledge. The atmosphere was calm and welcoming, a refreshing contrast to the bustle outside.✨️😇

The shelves are lined with beautifully printed Hindu scriptures and books– Bhagavad Gita, Ramcharitmanas, and many other timeless spiritual texts–all offered at very reasonable prices. The staff here are courteous, patient, and genuinely helpful, guiding visitors to the right editions or translations with humility. Their respectful approach adds to the sacred aura of the place.

What stands out most is the purity of purpose–Geeta Press has always been dedicated to spreading spiritual wisdom rather than commercial gain, and this branch reflects that ethos perfectly. It feels less like shopping and more like receiving blessings in the form of literature.

⚠️One practical note: parking in this area can be challenging due to narrow, crowded lanes. It’s often easier to reach by taxi or walking from nearby stations. But once inside, the serenity of the store makes you forget the outside chaos.

For anyone seeking authentic Hindu scriptures and spiritual books, along with a touch of old Mumbai charm, Geeta Press Gorakhpur at Princess Street is a treasure worth cherishing.
